<description>
The log escapes control characters so that a message cannot drive the terminal it is printed on, but it lets through the UTF-8 form of the C1 controls U+0080 to U+009F. VTE, the library behind GNOME Terminal and others, decodes these as CSI, OSC, DCS and the rest, like their `ESC [`, `ESC ]` and `ESC P` forms.

I escape the two-byte sequences 0xC2 0x80 to 0xC2 0x9F as `\xc2\x9b` and so on. Since 0xC2 is never a continuation byte, this needs no UTF-8 decoder, and all other non-ASCII text still passes untouched, as asked in #17095 and #35833. Single bytes 0x80 to 0x9F stay as they are, since they occur inside valid UTF-8. The new cases in `test_LogEscapeMessage` fail on master and pass with the change.
</description>

Tested on Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04), g++ 13.3.0, Release: `logging_tests` pass, also with this branch merged onto current master (de96f3ae). With U+009B and U+009F in a regtest datadir path, debug.log has `\xc2\x9b` and `\xc2\x9f` on this branch and the raw bytes on the merge-base.

Nit: the two new checks don't independently pin down both boundaries. Changing the lower bound to `>= 0x7f` or the end check to `i + 1 <= str.size()` still passes them. The trailing `\xc2` in the second check is a string literal, so `str[str.size()]` reads the terminating NUL.

Adding after line 141:

```cpp
BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(BCLog::LogEscapeMessage("\xc2\x7f"), "\xc2" R"(\x7f)");
BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(BCLog::LogEscapeMessage(std::string_view{"\xc2\x9b", 1}), "\xc2");
```

Both pass on this branch. Each fails only with its corresponding mutant (lines 142 and 143, respectively; Debian 13 x86_64, GCC 14.2.0, Release).

Nit: the `LogEscapeMessage` doc comment and the test comment "ASCII and UTF-8 must pass through unaltered" don't mention the C1 exception. Also, U+0100 isn't adjacent to the tested range: that case checks a different lead byte followed by `0x80`. The test itself is fine; only the comment is misleading.
